title: Descent of a connected open using a finite locally free multisection
statement: Let $f:X\to B$ and $p:Z\to B$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\sigma:Z\to X$ satisfy $f\circ\sigma=p$. Suppose that $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and that every fibre $X_b$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(b)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Suppose that $p$ is finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Let $b_0\in B$ satisfy $Z_{b_0}\ne\varnothing$ and suppose that $X_{b_0}$ is geometrically connected over $\kappa(b_0)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], where connected includes nonempty [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then there exists a quasi-compact open subscheme $X^0\subseteq X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] such that $X^0_{b_0}=X_{b_0}$ as open subschemes of $X_{b_0}$ and every nonempty fibre of $X^0\to B$ is geometrically connected over its residue field [def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: Put $Y=X\times_B Z$, $s=(\sigma,\mathrm{id}_Z):Z\to Y$, and $R=Z\times_B Z$ with structure map $q:R\to B$. Apply [lem-trf-multisection-component-overlap-neighbourhood] to $f,p,\sigma,b_0$; its hypotheses are given. It supplies an open $C\subseteq Y$ whose fibre at $z$ is the component containing $s(z)$, and an open $W\subseteq R$ containing $q^{-1}(b_0)$. For the induced projections $a_i:X\times_B R\to Y$ and $h:X\times_B R\to R$, its conclusion is $h^{-1}W\cap a_0^{-1}C=h^{-1}W\cap a_1^{-1}C$.

source.place: Tag 057I, lemma-descent-connected-fibres, proof; assembly of extracted arguments

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-invariant-component-affine-descent] to $f,p,\sigma,b_0,C,W$. The preceding equality verifies its compatibility hypothesis; $p$ is finite locally free and $Z_{b_0}$ is nonempty by assumption. It gives an affine neighbourhood $V$ of $b_0$ with $q^{-1}V\subseteq W$, affine $Z_V$, surjective finite locally free $p_V:Z_V\to V$, and a quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X_V$ satisfying $\pi^{-1}U=C_V$ for $\pi:X_V\times_V Z_V\to X_V$ and $C_V=C\times_B V$. Under the canonical identification $Y\times_B V\simeq X_V\times_V Z_V$, the restriction of $C\hookrightarrow Y$ is exactly $C_V\hookrightarrow X_V\times_V Z_V$; thus this pullback equality concerns the component open from step 1.

source.place: Tag 057I, lemma-descent-connected-fibres, proof; assembly of extracted arguments

proof.text: Use the fibre comparison [lem-trf-descended-section-component-field-fibres] over $V$, with $f_V:X_V\to V$, $p_V$, $C_V$ and $U$. The restricted multisection $\sigma_V:Z_V\to X_V$ is the morphism induced by $\sigma|_{Z_V}$ and $p_V$; its commuting equation $f_V\circ\sigma_V=p_V$ is the restriction of $f\circ\sigma=p$. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] preserves finite presentation under this base change, hence $f_V$ is locally of finite type: its finitely presented affine algebras have finite polynomial generators. Restriction to $V$ preserves the fibres and section points, so $(C_V)_z=C_z$ is the component containing $s(z)$; step 2 supplies the required surjectivity and pullback equality. For any $b\in V$, choose $z\in Z_V$ above $b$. The comparison makes $(U_b)_{\kappa(z)}$ geometrically connected over $\kappa(z)$, as the component of the $\kappa(z)$-rational section point. Reflect this by [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-check-after-extension] along $\kappa(z)/\kappa(b)$ to obtain geometric connectedness of $U_b$. At $b_0$, the comparison also gives $U_{b_0}=(X_V)_{b_0}=X_{b_0}$, since this original fibre is geometrically connected.

source.place: Tag 057I, lemma-descent-connected-fibres, proof; assembly of extracted arguments

proof.text: The open immersion $X_V\hookrightarrow X$ identifies $U$ with an open $X^0\subseteq X$. Its underlying space is still quasi-compact. For $b\in V$ its fibre is $U_b$, and for $b\notin V$ it is empty, by the fibre-product definition. Thus the designated fibre is unchanged and every nonempty fibre is geometrically connected.
